Johnson's algorithm reweights the edges to remove the negative one without changing which paths are shortest, then runs Dijkstra from every node. The path it returns from A to B is A, C, B (accent color), costing 2 + (−1) = 1, less than the direct edge's 4." width="100%"} Johnson's algorithm computes a shortest path between every pair of nodes on a graph that may have negative edge weights (but no negative cycles). It reweights the edges with node potentials so that all weights become non-negative without changing which paths are shortest, then runs Dijkstra's algorithm from every node. On sparse graphs it is much faster than `floyd_warshall()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, dict[int, list[int]]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `result[source][target]` is a shortest path as node IDs, for every reachable pair. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph has a negative cycle (or an undirected graph has a negative edge). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Bellman-Ford from a virtual source joined to every node gives potentials $h$ with $w'(u, v) = w(u, v) + h(u) - h(v) \ge 0$; every path's reweighted length differs from its true length by $h(s) - h(t)$, so shortest paths are preserved (Johnson, 1977). Total time $O(VE + V E \log V)$. Path lengths match NetworkX's `johnson`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#635eb40c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B", 4.0), ("A", "C", 2.0), ("C", "B", -1.0)]) paths = g.johnson() [g.get_label_from_id(n) for n in paths[g.get_id_from_label("A")][g.get_id_from_label("B")]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['A', 'C', 'B'] ``` ::: :::
